alalal-e89714-d1e104.summary: Rubric of Article 8: whether we are bound to believe things that are not articles.

alalal-e89714-d1e113.summary: States the fifth problem: whether we are bound to believe things that are not articles, and introduces arguments.

alalal-e89714-d1e122.summary: First argument: whoever does not believe fornication is a mortal sin is held a heretic, so its opposite belongs to faith and would be an article; likewise for other moral truths.

alalal-e89714-d1e145.summary: Second argument: some things are believed before faith, as Hebrews 11:6 requires believing that God exists and rewards in order to approach him.

alalal-e89714-d1e165.summary: Objection to saying that fornication's being mortal is an article while God's existence is not: the former is not a truth about God, so not an article.

alalal-e89714-d1e181.summary: Third argument: God's existence is in the creed as an article or part of one, so it is false that it precedes faith.
concepts: existence of God in the creed

alalal-e89714-d1e192.summary: Fourth: it constrains us to believe, so it is an article.

alalal-e89714-d1e199.summary: Fifth: it is an indivisible truth about God, so it is an article.

alalal-e89714-d1e206.summary: Sixth: whoever does not believe it is an unbeliever, so faith concerns it as an article.

alalal-e89714-d1e216.summary: Solution: as in other sciences there are principal and substantial truths, the main conclusions, and consequent truths, secondary conclusions and corollaries, as in geometry's suppositions, theorems and corollaries, so in faith. First must be supposed what believing God and believing God's word require, that God exists and that his words in Scripture are true: these are the suppositions and axioms. The articles are the principal conclusions; what pertains to good morals is like consequent corollaries. All must be believed by faith broadly taken.
claims: Faith has a structure like a science: God's existence and Scripture's truth as axioms, the articles as principal conclusions, and moral truths as corollaries.
Moral truths must be believed by faith, though they are not articles.

alalal-e89714-d1e264.summary: Reply to the second argument: this belongs to faith as believing that God is and believing God; faith that believes into God first approaches by tending toward him, and though these may be simultaneous in time, they are prior and posterior by nature.

alalal-e89714-d1e282.summary: Reply: as said, we believe many things by faith as consequences that are not principal articles.

alalal-e89714-d1e293.summary: Reply on believing that God is: articles are set according to believing that God is and believing into God, not according to believing God, which concerns understanding of Scripture, as hearing.
claims: Articles relate to credere Deum and in Deum, not to credere Deo, which concerns the truth of Scripture.

alalal-e89714.summary: Article 8 asks whether we must believe things that are not articles, such as that fornication is a mortal sin or that God exists. Albert models faith on a demonstrative science. Its suppositions or axioms are what believing God and his word require: that God exists and that Scripture is true. The articles are its principal conclusions, and moral truths are consequent corollaries. All of these must be believed by faith broadly taken, though only the articles are articles. Articles belong to believing that God is and believing into God, while believing God concerns the truth of Scripture received by hearing.
claims: Faith includes axioms (God's existence and Scripture's truth), principal conclusions (the articles) and corollaries (moral truths).
Moral truths must be believed, though they are not articles.
Articles concern credere Deum and in Deum; credere Deo concerns the truth of Scripture.
